x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: average attendance at the 16 DRSCs and the PAC was only 53% since the September reconstitution, and five meetings were postponed for lack of quorum. Statement 3 is the trap: the notes give no basis for saying the PAC held no meeting; it is one of the committees whose (low) attendance was measured. Hence '1 and 2 only'.

The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha committee has 10. The 22-member elected pattern belongs to PAC/COPU, option C reverses the two figures, and 31 members is the size of a DRSC.

A is true: the PAC chairman has been an Opposition member since 1967. R is false: this is a convention, not a constitutional or statutory rule applicable in every case. Hence 'A is true but R is false'.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct: under Art. 163(2) the Governor's decision on whether a matter is discretionary is final, and Art. 163(3) bars courts from inquiring into ministers' advice. Statement 2 is false: his acts cannot be questioned on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
All four pairs match the notes: Chandrababu Naidu was CM 2014-19, Jagan Mohan Reddy 2019-24, Chandrababu Naidu again from June 2024, and S. Abdul Nazeer has been Governor since February 2023.

A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III: Goswami (1990) would disqualify only for voluntarily giving up membership or defying the whip on confidence/no-confidence motions; the Law Commission's 170th Report (1999) would delete the split and merger exceptions and treat pre-poll alliances as parties; NCRWC (2002) would bar defectors from public or remunerative political office for the rest of the term and treat their votes as invalid; the EC wanted the President/Governor to decide on its binding advice. Option B swaps B and C; options C and D misplace Goswami and the EC.

Executive-legislature deadlock and the danger of a personality cult around a single executive are demerits of the presidential system. Statements 3 and 4 are wrong: the presidential executive has a fixed tenure (its merit), while lack of fixed tenure and unstable coalitions are demerits of the parliamentary system. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
